- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often over-anticipates decline; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent range.
- Model consistently under-responds to sharp sentiment reversals (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33); add 0.5–1.5x the magnitude of sentiment shift to correct lag.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 70, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until price stabilizes; if below 65, increase by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates volatility in sentiment-neutral periods; reduce forecast variance by 15–20% if sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33) over 5+ days.
- If sentiment history shows “+0.67, -0.33, +0.67” pattern, model often fails to capture second +0.67 spike; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast 2–3 days after sentiment turns positive.
